newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar ends firmer after volatile trade.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar ends firmer after volatile trade.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar closed firmer at 479.50/480.75 per dollar after some uncharacteristically wild gyrating confused traders who saw the unit soar in opening trade to 491 and then drop as low as 476.
"It was crazy," said one trader, adding that the only reason he saw for the volatility was a Central Bank attempt to discourage speculation.
"The bolivar surged ahead in the morning, upto 491 per dollar," said another trader. "Then the Central Bank came in, and pushed the rate down, punishing anyone who had taken positions."
The volatility appeared to mark a sea-change in the Central Bank's approach to the foreign exchange market, brokers said.
Previously, sessions had taken place within narrow trading ranges, informally set by the Bank in light of the fact it is the far and away the country's largest single seller of dollars.
By law, state-owned oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) must sell all its petro-dollars to the Bank.
